**$q$-bit.** The elementary unit of information in a quantum observable universe with aether parameter $q$, defined as the operational entropy $\eta_q = (2q - 1)/q^3$ generated by a single crossing resolution in $H_n(q)$ between the symmetric eigenvalue $q$ and the antisymmetric eigenvalue $-q^{-1}$ (see [operational entropy](#def:operational-entropy)); this unit is called one :defterm[$q$-bit]{#q-bit}. At the classical limit $q = 1$, the two eigenvalues merge in magnitude to $\pm 1$ and $\eta_1 = 1$ recovers one classical nat, whereas $\eta_q \to 0$ in the deep-quantum limit $q \to \infty$.
